attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his Substack post, written in his own voice. He is not quoting anyone else.

semantics.note: This is a firm present-tense observation. 'A lot of' and 'somewhat underwhelmed' are kept. ChatGPT is the product implied by the context, and the contract flags that ambiguity.

contract.note: The plain reading is fair and ordinary: a substantial group of companies, not necessarily a majority, is mildly disappointed. Allowing evidence on GPT-powered Copilot is reasonable given the context. The contradiction bar, that disappointment was rare, is fair.

evidence.note: Business Insider reports one unnamed large customer calling Copilot tools gimmicky. One unnamed firm cannot show Fortune 500 membership or how common the view is.
The BCG survey covers AI broadly across global firms. Not yet showing value is not the same as being disappointed with ChatGPT, and the survey does not isolate Fortune 500 firms.

Gartner IT-leader survey as reported by Computerworld, available before the cutoff. Its mixed findings on Copilot value do not single out Fortune 500 firms or measure disappointment against expectations.

reviews.rationale: No item in the packet identifies Fortune 500 companies and measures their disappointment with ChatGPT or GPT tools. e1 is one unnamed firm. e2 covers AI too broadly. e3's mixed Copilot findings neither establish nor refute a substantial disappointed group. The evidence does not settle the claim.
